alternate_names: Thikana Mandir Shri Govind Dev Ji

history.summary: Built in 1735 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, the founder of Jaipur, within the City Palace complex (Jai Niwas Garden, Jalebi Chowk). The deity Govind Dev Ji is believed to be the exact image of Krishna: legend says the idol was sculpted by Bajranabh, the great-grandson of Krishna, and was brought to Jaipur from Vrindavan by Sawai Jai Singh II to protect it from the religiously intolerant Mughal emperor Aurangzeb. It was the principal deity of the Kachwaha rulers; the temple's position allowed the Maharaja a direct view from Chandra Mahal. The idol is unveiled seven times daily for aartis. The complex includes gardens and a Hanuman shrine at the rear.

name: Govind Dev Ji Temple
town_description: Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan, is the 'Pink City' — founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, its rose-hued walled old city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the historic heart of Kachwaha Rajput culture, home to the City Palace, Hawa Mahal and Jantar Mantar.

travel.airport: Jaipur International Airport, about 12 km away (verify).
travel.railway: Jaipur Junction railway station, about 3 km away (verify).
travel.road: Inside the City Palace complex at Jalebi Chowk, old city; reachable by auto-rickshaw, taxi and city bus.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Janmashtami draws the largest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open roughly 4:30 AM-12:00 PM and 5:45 PM-9:30 PM; the idol is unveiled at seven daily aartis (mangala, dhoop, shringar, rajbhog, gwal, sandhya, shayan).
